findings.body: The previous finding remains open. The GitHub query retrieves headRefOid, but this failure override never compares it with the local branch head. After a repair commit, a cached or freshly fetched failure for the previous push still makes tasks and fixes show checks failed and recommend forge work instead of forge close in both machine views. Keep displaying the PR's checks, but apply their failure to local readiness only when they describe the current head.
findings.title: Ignore previous-head failures when deriving the local next step

findings.body: The previous finding remains open. The machine board fetches only open PRs and passes an empty merged-PR set here. Tasks and fixes merged on GitHub therefore retain their previous stage and merge advice until origin/main is fetched; story next steps also overlook those merges. The existing next-step implementation obtains merged branches at src/forge/nextstep.py:189 and applies them to fixes at lines 208–209 and tasks at lines 506–516. Use that evidence consistently in the machine board.
findings.title: Recognize GitHub merges before the default branch is fetched

findings.body: The previous finding remains open. The live stage includes only runs without an end record, so a second attempt replaces the first attempt's start and resets its timer. Claude and Codex commit nudges launch another run within the same round at src/forge/worker.py:193–199 and 212–219; review retries do likewise at src/forge/review.py:464–470. Build and Review lose elapsed time during that attempt, then jump back when the full timing is recorded. Anchor the stage to its first recorded start in the current round while retaining the active worker's own start.
findings.title: Preserve the live stage's start across attempts in one round
